resources.string: Keeps the swap off anything in front of the face: food, hands, cups, a microphone, hair. Uses the XSeg model on the GPU or CPU.
Swaps only skin, eyes, brows, nose and lips (BiSeNet). Hair, ears and neck stay original.
Teeth, tongue and whatever is in the mouth stay as filmed. Best for eating and talking.
The lips also stay as filmed, so the whole mouth is the real one. Most natural while eating or with the mouth wide open; the lips are then the original person\'s, not the source face\'s.
The app closed unexpectedly last time, because of %1$s. If it happens again, try the Fast preset, 30 fps or a shorter trim, and share a bug report (Settings, About).
Your last video is reloaded and all your settings are kept. If the app closes again, try switching off Faster masks (Face Masker) or using 256 pixel boost for that video.
"%1$s" was stopped at %2$s of %3$s. Continue from where it stopped? The same video, trim and output settings are used.
"%1$s" is swapped up to %2$s of %3$s and can still be continued. Swapping this other video replaces it, and its swapped part is deleted. To keep it, cancel and tap Continue unfinished swap first.
Works out the masks on the graphics chip while the AI chip swaps the face, at the same time. Faster with the masks on, same result.

Videos only: skips work a frame does not need. The masks are reused while nothing moves in front of the face, the expression restorer runs around blinks and closed eyes, and "Keep original mouth inside" works only while the mouth is open. Faster, cooler, almost always the same result. Previews and photos always do everything.
Fast: quick and still good. 256 pixel boost, occlusion mask, skin-tone matching; no enhancer, expression restorer or mouth masks. Also set Output settings to 30 fps for 60 fps videos.

Sets everything for the most natural result: 512 pixel boost, occlusion mask, real mouth inside, skin-tone matching, expression restorer, face enhancer at half strength, head-turn fade, motion smoothing. Slower. Keeps your model, faces and output settings.
The swapped face takes the skin tone and lighting of the video, so it does not look pasted on.
Puts the original expression back on the swapped face: closed eyes, blinking, mouth shape. Uses the face editor models (download them in Settings, Models). Adds time per face.
Fade out on big head turns
When the head turns too far left, right, up or down for the swapper, the original face shows through smoothly instead of a stretched one.
Head turn where the fade begins. The swap is gone 20° later. Lower is safer, higher keeps more of the swap.
Video and Live: steadies the face alignment between frames and keeps motion-blurred faces swapped during fast movement.
Also looks for heads turned sideways or upside down (90°, 180°, 270°). Slower on frames without a face.
Hair (and hats) always stay as filmed, and the edge of the swap follows the real edges in the picture, so strands across the face never turn into dark streaks. Uses the face parser.
Blends the swapped face into the video\'s own skin at the edge, so there is no outline at the forehead, cheeks or jaw.
A face shown big in the frame is swapped at 1024 pixels instead of being stretched, so its edges stay clean. Takes longer on close-ups only.

Videos: the skin tone, the edge of the swap and the swapped face itself change gently from frame to frame instead of flickering, also while hands or food pass in front of the face. Real movement (the mouth opening, a turn) is not smoothed.

Recommended settings are on: face parser with hair-aware and seamless edges, close-up detail, occlusion mask, real mouth inside, skin tone, expression restorer 80, enhancer 50, smoothing, 30 fps and 1080p for 4K. Change anything in the gear on face_swapper.

Each face can have up to 5 photos of the same person (front, left, right, up, down). They are combined into one likeness, and for every frame the photo whose head angle matches the video counts most. Assign faces to the people in a video on the Swap tab (Assign per person).

Best photos: sharp, well lit, nothing over the face. One straight on, one turned left, one turned right, then up and down. Or tap From a video and the app picks the best ones for you. Each photo says if something is wrong with it.

Photos of the same person are combined into one likeness. For every frame the photo whose head angle matches the face in the video counts most (turned left: your left-turned photo), blending smoothly as the head turns. Add one straight on, one turned left, one turned right, then up and down.
Best: sharp, well lit, nothing over the face; one straight on, one turned left, one turned right, then up and down.
This phone could not run the %1$s models, so the %2$s set is used instead.
With the lip syncer on, it drives the mouth and these sliders are ignored.
Each slider runs from -1 to 1. At 0 the face is unchanged.
Builds the GPU and CPU models in a way that needs less memory, for phones with 6 GB or less. Slightly slower.
It is on for this phone.
It is off for this phone.
Use the mirror if Hugging Face is slow or blocked where you are.
FaceFusion Mobile is free. If it is useful to you, you can support its development.

The app checks about two frames a second and keeps the sharpest, best lit picture of each angle. Nothing is swapped.
Who should be added? Tap a person.
The best pictures it found. Tap to tick or untick, then Add.
This person was not found in the video (or only too small).
No clear face was found in the video.
The video has no angle this face does not already have.
Adds crispness to the enhanced face (skin texture, eyes). Off by default; too much looks artificial.
Keeps fewer frames in memory while swapping. Same result, a little slower. Turn on only if the phone closes the app.
Test of 3 seconds ready. Happy with it? Press Swap for the whole video.
phone gets hot, the app slows down to protect it
About %1$s (rough guess until your first swap) · %2$s
The unfinished swap could not be found any more. Press Swap to start again.
Save the part that is done
The part that is already swapped is deleted and cannot be continued. Your faces and settings stay.
The first %1$s are saved as a video below. The unfinished swap is still there to continue.
This removes the video, the result and any unfinished swap. Your faces and settings stay.
New project: pick a video to start.
Waiting for the models to finish loading, then the swap starts… (Cancel stops it)
Lip sync needs a voice: add one or switch lip sync off.
While an eye is shut, its own lids and lashes stay as filmed, so they do not smear. Each eye on its own (winks too).
Swap turned faces with side photos
If this person has a photo turned the same way (Faces tab), a face turned sideways keeps the swap 15 degrees further round before fading.

On a turned face the swapper draws a front face, so it invents the far eye and the nose outline (an eye on the cheek, a nose edge). From 35 degrees of turn the swap is kept on the visible half only, up to the nose line; the far side stays as filmed, fully from 60 degrees. The mouth and the visible cheek and eye keep the swap; front faces are unchanged.

Everything for food, spoons, forks and fingers at the mouth, in one tap: Strongest likeness, plus the lips follow the filmed mouth while biting and chewing, in exactly the source\'s lipstick colour; food and hands stay as filmed; the real teeth and food stay inside the mouth; soft edges, smooth over time, side guard, a light enhancer. As fast as Strongest likeness.

Makes the face look as much like the source photo as possible: stronger weight, the face parser only keeps hair (it no longer cuts the swap to the original face outline), the source\'s mouth with Lips auto and Lipstick match, and the expression restorer on the mouth only. Slower than the default.

The first clear view of each person is swapped at your weight and at +0.1 and +0.2, and the lowest one that looks most like the source is used for that person for the whole video. A few extra swaps per person, once.

The swapped face takes the video\'s light and shadow direction (one side brighter, the other darker), not only its overall colour. More natural in side light, but the original\'s shading also carries a little of their face shape, so likeness drops slightly. Cheap.
Saves the swapped video at twice the bitrate, so fine detail (skin, lashes, the enhancer\'s sharpness) survives the compression. Bigger files; no extra processing.

The restorer moves the mouth fully like the original (open, chewing, around food) and the rest of the face only lightly, so the face keeps more of the source. Also runs while the mouth is open, not only on blinks.
The lips stay the source\'s, except the band that food, a fork, a spoon or a cup touches, which stays as filmed. Needs the occlusion mask.
Match the video\'s grain and sharpness

The finished face takes the video\'s own fine detail: a swapped face that is sharper than the face it replaces is softened to it, and one that is smoother gets the video\'s own grain. A face whose texture does not belong to the footage is what gives a swap away. No model, no extra time worth naming.
Fill frames where the face is lost

Video only. When the face finder loses a face for a few frames (blur, a hand, a quick turn) and finds it again within the next 5 frames, the face is carried through the gap instead of being left as filmed. The swap looks a few frames ahead for this; frames where every face is found cost nothing extra.

The lips and the open mouth keep the video\'s own shape, so they are always exactly in line with the filmed mouth, and the swapped lips never spill onto the skin around them. With Lipstick match they take the source photo\'s lip colour.
Lips kept as filmed take the source photo\'s lip colour (lipstick or natural) with their own shading, and swapped lips are brought towards it. Food and teeth are never coloured.
The face parser keeps only hair and hats as filmed and does not cut the swap down to the original face outline, so hair edges stay clean and the face keeps more of the source.
When a face that was on screen a moment ago is lost (turned, half hidden, blurred), or no face is found at all, a second detector looks too. Frames where every face is found cost nothing extra.
Second face-point model for turned faces (PEPPA-Wutz)

For a face the normal face-point model is unsure of (turned, tilted, blurred), a second one places the eyes, nose and mouth too, and the more confident one is used. Faces it is sure of cost nothing extra.
A more exact outline of skin, hair and ears for the face parser mask. About twice the parser\'s work (measured); off keeps the speed as before.

Restores the face at 512 px instead of 256: twice the detail on close-ups, but several times the enhancer\'s work, so swaps are slower and use more battery. Needs the phone\'s NPU; off keeps everything as before.
Every person who appears, from the first second to the last, is listed once. Works for any length of video; a long film takes a few minutes. Keep the app open.
Scan only part of the video
Only this part is searched for people, to save time. Anyone you assign is still swapped everywhere they appear, from the beginning of the video to the end.
The swap covers only %1$s to %2$s (the trim above). Assigned people are swapped from the beginning to the end of that part.
Person %1$d and person %2$d are now one person.

%1$d people in this video. One picture per person. Pick a photo for each one; it is used for that person from the start of the video to the end. Tap ✕ to drop someone you do not want, or Same person as… if one person is listed twice.
Nobody was found in this video.
Anyone not assigned keeps their own face
Anyone not assigned gets the source picked when you turned this on
